text.insert: Decision: storage/ddl.ts is the schema authority. Every schema change must update storage/schema.ts, the ordered migrations where required, and the fresh-store parity test in storage/schema.test.ts. Why: DDL carries CHECK constraints while the typed mirror supports queries; an outdated mirror hides schema drift. Applies to: every future table, column, and named index. The test compares table and column sets and verifies every declared named index exists.

Decision: model-produced semantic proposals go through apply before facts, evidence, links, or curated entities change. The model never receives a writable store handle. Why: shape, scope, citation, and overwrite checks share one implementation. Applies to: librarian, backfill, and future semantic model writers. Deterministic reconciliation and citation re-anchoring have their own bounded maintenance contracts.
: the index database is derived and disposable; nothing reads it as truth and every build is a full replacement per table.
: search quality changes with chunking and models; a rebuild must be free.
: knowledge jobs are CLIs inside their owning module, dispatched by the application job runner as kg2-*.
: the dispatcher stays a routing table and each job's flags live beside the code they drive.

Decision: core/knowledge keeps the code graph, its builders and jobs, and authored standards used by current callers. The V1 learnings ledger, classification lane, learnings API, and legacy dashboard are retired; frozen V1 data is historical archive material. Why: graph retrieval still has active users while V2 owns semantic knowledge and attempt records. Applies to: apps/server/src/core/knowledge; new knowledge behavior belongs in knowledge-v2.
